verdicts.reason: Both share the same broken leaderboard structure: the green circle is cropped at the left edge and split from the tiny can, whose SOLSTICE label is illegible, the wordmark sits below the headline, and the CTA is jammed at the front of the badge row. A sets the body copy in 2 readable-ish lines, while B squeezes it into a cramped 4-line sliver of microscopic text.

Same flaws as pair 1: the cropped decorative circle is orphaned on the left, the can is a tiny unreadable icon floating far right, the brand sits under the headline, and the CTA is buried in the pill row at about the same weight as the badges. A's 2-line body copy is marginally more legible than B's 4-line column of tiny text.

A puts the can on the left, so the image-then-text reading order of the original comes back, but the can still floats beside the cropped circle instead of on it and a large dead zone opens on the right. B leaves the can stranded far right with the 4-line microscopic body copy. Both have the brand under the headline and an undersized CTA.

A gives the body copy its own full-width line, which reads better, but stacks headline, wordmark, copy and buttons with no breathing room, and its CTA and pills shrink to tiny sizes. B has the cramped 4-line microscopic body copy and the same orphaned circle and tiny far-right can. Neither is shippable.
